title: The Normalization of Deviance in AI Development
abstract: arXiv:2609.05749v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Work on the risks of artificial intelligence has focused predominantly on capability risk: the danger that systems become too powerful, too autonomous, or too misaligned with human values. Far less attention has been paid to the organizational level---to whether the institutions building these systems are themselves predisposed to drift toward failure. This paper argues that they are. Regardless of how capable AI systems become, the organizations building them face the same structural dynamics that preceded past major technological disasters. Drawing on case studies of the Space Shuttle Challenger, the Three Mile Island accident, and the Boeing 737 MAX crashes, this paper identifies the common structural mechanisms preceding each failure and maps them onto contemporary AI development. translated_title: 人工智能开发中的偏差常态化
translated_abstract: 关于人工智能风险的研究主要集中于能力风险：即系统变得过于强大、过于自主或与人类价值观偏离过远的危险。而对组织层面的关注却少得多——即构建这些系统的机构本身是否也容易逐渐滑向失败。本文认为，事实确实如此。无论人工智能系统变得多么强大，构建它们的组织都面临着与过去重大技术灾难发生前相同的结构性动态。本文通过对挑战者号航天飞机、三里岛核事故和波音737 MAX坠机事件的案例研究，识别出每次失败之前共同存在的结构性机制，并将其映射到当代人工智能开发中。研究结果表明，现有的安全基础设施所提供的保护可能比表面看起来要少，因为组织可能会草率地走完安全流程……
tldr: 本文通过分析挑战者号航天飞机、三里岛核事故和波音737 MAX等历史技术灾难案例，指出人工智能开发组织正在重蹈“偏差常态化”的覆辙，现有的安全机制所提供的保护可能远不及表面看起来那么可靠。
en_tdlr: Drawing on case studies of the Challenger disaster, Three Mile Island, and the Boeing 737 MAX crashes, this paper argues that AI development organizations are subject to the same structural dynamics of deviance normalization that preceded past technological disasters, suggesting existing safety infrastructure may provide far less protection than it appears.
